answer: Sybil resistance rests on one mechanism: a per-identity bond that matures only after an orchard of consecutive honest epochs, so a farm cannot be spun up and cashed out in a night. Each epoch rotating peers attest, and duplicate registrations from one operator collapse onto shared device fingerprints, slashing every bond at once. A thousand clones cost a thousand bonds while payout per clone stays flat, and registration also needs a unique proof-of-work inlet, so marginal revenue turns negative. A zephyr of fresh identities buys nothing when capital, not count, is the scarce input.
